methodology.record_note: CANTO predicts the complete native AhmedML surface and volume fields from the NURBS description of the body. The geometry input is a 13-patch, 72-control-point NURBS net plus its level-4 subdivided anchor net; the native meshes supply cell-centroid positions only, as query points and as volume anchor positions, and never field data. Predictions come from actual inference with the single checkpoint declared below, decoded at every native cell in source order, so no interpolation or mapping is applied before scoring. The model was trained from scratch on 399 AhmedML cases, none of them among the 50 Full test cases (run_500 was not used), and monitored on 50 further validation cases. The declared checkpoint, model.pt, is the last checkpoint written by the single training run, at optimizer step 86000 of a 100000-step cosine schedule: the tenth four-hour training job reached its time limit after writing it, and the run was not resubmitted because the validation loss had plateaued. Contact with the public test cases: the training configuration enabled test-split evaluation, so test-split metrics were computed and logged alongside the validation metrics every ten epochs. Before this package was assembled, the run's validation-selected checkpoint (model_best.pt, tracked on validation surface-pressure relative L2) was also run on the same 50 test cases and scored with the candidate evaluator; that result is not submitted. The submitter states that submitting the final checkpoint was decided before any test-split score was seen, that test-split metrics did not influence training, stopping or checkpoint selection, and that every normalisation statistic was computed from training cases only.

architecture.description: Two-stage model. A Perceiver-style NURBS geometry encoder pools the control net of each patch into latent tokens using bucketed variable-length attention over control points together with learned embeddings of the two knot vectors, then refines those tokens with latent self-attention. An anchored branched transformer (AB-UPT) conditions on the resulting geometry tokens: a shared trunk is followed by separate surface and volume branches, each of which first predicts at a set of anchor positions and then lets arbitrary query points attend to those anchors. Surface anchors are patch centroids of a subdivided NURBS net and volume anchors are native volume cell centroids drawn from the query set. Query points are never attention keys, so any number of them can be decoded in chunks without changing the result. Control points and query coordinates share one union min/max normalisation frame.

Anchored surface branch. Predicts at NURBS patch-centroid anchors, then decodes arbitrary surface query points by attention to those anchors.

data_handling.normalization: Surface output channels are standardised by the per-channel mean and standard deviation stored in surface_flow_stats.pt, and volume output channels by those stored in volume_flow_stats_with_cpt.pt. These files, the coordinate statistics in volume_coords_stats.pt and the NURBS input statistics in inputs_NURBS_stats.pt were all computed from training cases only. Control points and query coordinates share one union min/max frame; the loaded input statistics carry mean and standard deviation but no control-point bounds, so the frame falls back to the query-coordinate bounds in volume_coords_stats.pt, which is the code path the checkpoint was trained under. Predictions are denormalised to physical units before being written, so the evaluator receives raw dataset units.
data_handling.preprocessing: Training reads HDF5 shards converted once from the public VTP and VTU files, carrying cell-centroid coordinates, cell areas, surface normals and field values; the volume shards hold every native volume cell in shuffled order. Inference therefore takes its query positions straight from the published VTP and VTU files, recomputing each native cell centroid by averaging the cell's vertices, which matches how the training coordinates were produced and handles the polyhedral volume cells. Geometry and anchor nets come from the NURBS archives. No remeshing, decimation or smoothing is applied at any stage.
data_handling.sampling: Training draws 16384 surface queries, 16384 volume anchors and 16384 volume queries per geometry at every step, uniformly from the case's native cells, and drops 10 percent of the surface anchors. Inference does not subsample the outputs: every native surface and volume cell is decoded exactly once in source order, in chunks of 2000000 queries, each against the same geometry and anchor context. The 16384 volume anchor positions are drawn once per case from the native volume centroids, from a random generator seeded with 0 at the start of each of the four inference worker processes, which take the cases round-robin in run-number order.

stages.description: Single joint stage training all components end to end from random initialisation on 399 AhmedML training cases, with 50 validation cases monitored every ten epochs. No pretraining and no staged freezing.

loss.description: Mean squared error between standardised predictions and targets at the sampled surface and volume query points. The surface target has four channels (pressure and three wall-shear-stress components); the volume target has eight (pressure, three velocity components, three vorticity components and the total-pressure coefficient), of which vorticity and total-pressure coefficient are auxiliary outputs that are not submitted.
loss.weighting: Surface loss plus 0.2 times volume loss; all channels within each term carry equal weight.

optimizers.name: Lion
optimizers.schedule: Linear warmup over 1000 steps, then cosine annealing to 1e-6 over a 100000-step horizon. Betas (0.9, 0.99), weight decay 0.05, gradient-norm clipping at 1.0, full fp32 precision.

compute.hardware: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3, eight GPUs on one node per job
compute.measurement_notes: One training run executed as ten consecutive single-node jobs of eight GPUs, each resuming from the previous rolling checkpoint and ending at its four-hour time limit; the experiment tracker recorded eight NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 devices for every job. Elapsed campaign time runs from the first job's start (2026-09-08T13:24Z) to the last job's end (about 2026-09-10T06:33Z), about 41.2 hours, including queue gaps of a few minutes between most jobs and about one hour between the sixth and seventh, during which no devices were held. Aggregate device time sums the actual allocations, ten jobs of four hours on eight GPUs, which is 320 GPU-hours; the tracker's cumulative process runtime is 39.8 hours, about 319 GPU-hours. Both include job start-up, dependency installation, checkpoint input and output, and the validation and test-split monitoring evaluations every ten epochs. The last job trained about 150 steps past the declared step-86000 checkpoint before its time limit; that work is included. Earlier exploratory runs and hyperparameter search are not counted.

checkpoints.bytes_description: The exact 51507803-byte PyTorch checkpoint file (model.pt) loaded for every case in this submission, containing the state dictionary of all four components of the single joint model. It is byte-identical to the run's rolling step-86000 checkpoint.
checkpoints.role: joint_surface_and_volume_model
checkpoints.selection_rule: The last checkpoint written by the single training run (model.pt, optimizer step 86000), not the run's validation-selected checkpoint (model_best.pt). The rule to submit the final checkpoint was fixed before any test-split score was seen, and the run was not resubmitted after its tenth job because the validation loss had plateaued.

inference_compute.hardware: NVIDIA GB200, four GPUs on one node
inference_compute.measurement_notes: One scheduler job on one node with four GPUs; the fifty cases were dealt round-robin to four worker processes, one per GPU. Wall time is the job's elapsed time and includes container dependency installation, checkpoint and geometry loading, and writing about 25 GB of prediction chunks to shared storage, so it overstates pure forward-pass cost. Aggregate device time is wall time multiplied by the four allocated GPUs, idle time included. Mapping is the identity because every native cell is decoded directly, so no separate mapping cost exists. Native cell-centroid extraction from the published VTP and VTU files ran earlier as a separate CPU job and is excluded. The export job did not log device names; the GPU model is reported by the submitter, and a job on the same partition that day recorded four NVIDIA GB200 devices.

methodology.record_note: Adapted from the official Transolver++ reference implementation (https://github.com/thuml/Transolver_plus/blob/main/models/Transolver_plus.py). Submitter-reported DDP adaptation note: the original implementation uses sequence parallelism (dist_nn.all_reduce inside Physics_Attention_1D_Eidetic) to synchronize attention tokens across devices, assuming one large spatial graph partitioned across GPUs. This pipeline instead uses standard Distributed Data Parallelism: because AirfRANS meshes have highly variable node counts (preventing batch stacking), each GPU processes exactly one intact mesh per step, so the entire graph for a sample fits in one GPU's VRAM. Leaving the cross-GPU all_reduce active under this DDP setup would aggregate attention tokens across independent meshes on different GPUs, cross-contaminating physical/geometric features between unrelated samples. The submitter therefore bypassed the dist_nn.all_reduce synchronization in the forward pass; global synchronization is instead handled correctly and exclusively by the DDP backend during the backward pass (gradient reduction), preserving strict per-sample independence in the forward computation. find_unused_parameters=True was set in the DDP wrapper to handle the idle condition-embedding layer present in the original architecture without structural deletions. Inference note: Physics_Attention_1D_Eidetic samples Gumbel noise in its slice weights even in eval mode, so the inference script reseeds torch (seed 42) before every case's forward pass; predictions are bit-for-bit reproducible per case.

methodology.record_note: CANTO predicts the complete native DrivAerML surface and volume fields from the NURBS description of each car. The geometry input is the case's set of untrimmed rectangular NURBS patches converted from the public DrivAerML CAD (43156 to 45647 patches and 6.5 to 7.4 million control points per test case); every patch token also serves as a surface anchor. The native meshes supply cell-centre positions only, as query points and, for 16384 volume cells per case, as volume anchor positions, and never field data. Predictions come from actual inference with the single checkpoint declared below, decoded at every native cell in source order, so no interpolation or mapping is applied before scoring. The model was trained from scratch on the 400 cases of the official Full training split, none of them among the 50 test cases, and evaluated during training on the 34 official validation cases only; no test-split metric was computed during training. The declared checkpoint, model.pt, is the last checkpoint written by the single training run, at optimizer step 200500: the run continued at the 1e-6 floor learning rate for 500 steps after its 200000-step cosine schedule ended, until the 21st four-hour job reached its time limit 24 seconds after writing this checkpoint, and it was not resubmitted. Code provenance: the run used a working tree whose uncommitted edits were later committed as aie-cfd 4a64903 (with aie-core 2bfd2f1). Configuration, algorithm and dataset files were edited during the run, before its last two jobs (steps 180000 to 200500); the earlier tree is not recoverable, but the recipe, optimizer and schedule are identical before and after, and inference parses the recorded configuration and loads the checkpoint with strict key matching. No random seed was set for training; see the training stage. GPU inference is not bitwise reproducible: the model sums per-patch control-point centroids with CUDA atomic additions, whose order varies between runs, and runs under bf16 autocast. Exporting run_11 a second time with the same volume anchors changed the surface predictions by a median of 0.14 percent (pressure) and 0.47 percent (wall shear stress) of the field RMS, its metric values by at most 0.17 percent relative and its drag coefficient by 0.00008; the submitted run_11 prediction is the second export. Every normalisation constant that affects the model equals its value computed from the training cases alone, as checked by recomputation (see data handling).

architecture.description: Two-stage model. A Perceiver-style NURBS geometry encoder turns each patch into one token: bucketed variable-length attention pools the patch's control points into 32 latents, separate pools encode its u and v knot vectors, and an MLP projects the concatenated latents to a single 192-wide token; six self-attention blocks then refine the patch tokens, about 44000 per case. An anchored branched transformer (AB-UPT) conditions on these geometry tokens: a shared trunk is followed by separate surface and volume branches, each of which predicts at a set of anchor positions and then lets arbitrary query points attend to those anchors. The patch tokens double as surface anchors, positioned at each patch's control-point centroid, and the volume anchors are 16384 native volume cell centres. Query points are never attention keys, so any number of them can be decoded in chunks. Control points and query coordinates share one union min/max normalisation frame.

components.description: Bucketed variable-length Perceiver pool over each patch's control points (32 latents, width 192, 3 heads, depth 2) with separate u and v knot-vector pools (4 latents, width 64, 2 heads, depth 1), an MLP projecting the 6656 pooled values to one 192-wide token per patch, and six self-attention blocks over the patch tokens. Produces the geometry token set consumed by every downstream branch.
Shared AB-UPT trunk applied to geometry tokens before the surface and volume branches diverge.

Anchored surface branch. Embeds the patch-centroid anchor positions, predicts at those anchors, then decodes arbitrary surface query points by attention to them. Outputs pressure and three wall-shear-stress components.

Anchored volume branch. Predicts at the sampled volume anchors, then decodes arbitrary volume query points by attention to them. Its decoder has eight output channels, of which only the first four (total-pressure coefficient and three velocity components) are supervised and used.

data_handling.normalization: Surface output channels (pressure and three wall-shear-stress components) are standardised by the per-channel mean and standard deviation in surface_flow_stats.pt, and volume output channels (total-pressure coefficient and three velocity components) by those in volume_flow_stats_with_cpt.pt. Recomputing over the 400 official training cases reproduces the surface statistics bit for bit, and the volume flow and coordinate statistics were written by the same training-only pass. Control points and query coordinates share one min/max frame, the union of the training volume-coordinate bounds (volume_coords_stats.pt) and the control-point bounds in the NURBS statistics file. That file came from a scan that included non-training archives (its x minimum comes from validation run 150, and its moments best match a scan of all 488 archives, test cases included), but the frame takes only its lower z bound, -0.9072 m, which training run 437 attains and which therefore equals the training-only value; every other frame bound comes from the volume coordinates, and the file's means and standard deviations are not used. Predictions are de-standardised to physical units before being written, so the evaluator receives raw dataset units.
data_handling.preprocessing: Training reads HDF5 shards converted once from the public VTP and VTU files, carrying cell-centre coordinates and field values for every native surface and volume cell in a once-shuffled row order; the volume shards also carry the total-pressure coefficient. Inference takes its query positions straight from the pinned native VTP and VTU files, recomputing the cell centres exactly as the conversion did (surface: VTK cell centres; volume: mean of each cell's vertices); for every test case the sorted centres equal the training-format coordinates exactly. Geometry comes from the per-case NURBS archives: untrimmed rectangular patches in metres converted from the public DrivAerML CAD. No remeshing, decimation or smoothing is applied at any stage.
data_handling.sampling: Training visits each of the 400 training cases once per epoch (one case per GPU per step, four GPUs, 100 steps per epoch). At every visit it takes three independent blocks of 16384 rows, each a contiguous block at a uniform random offset in the case's once-shuffled arrays: surface queries, volume anchors and volume queries; it also drops 20 percent of the surface anchor tokens. No random seed was set. Inference does not subsample the outputs: every native surface and volume cell is decoded exactly once in source order, in chunks of 2000000 queries, each chunk a full forward pass against the same geometry and anchor context. The 16384 volume anchors are drawn once per case from the native volume cell centres by a GPU random permutation seeded with the case's run number.

stages.description: Single joint stage training all components end to end from random initialisation on the 400 cases of the official Full training split, with the 34 official validation cases evaluated every five epochs. No pretraining and no staged freezing. No random seed was set: the configuration's seed is None and the trainer seeds only when a value is given, so each of the 21 jobs started from fresh entropy-seeded generator states. The schema requires one integer per stochastic run, so random_seeds holds -1 as a sentinel meaning not set; it is not a seed.

loss.description: Mean squared error between standardised predictions and targets at the sampled surface and volume query points. The surface target has four channels (pressure and three wall-shear-stress components); the volume target has four (total-pressure coefficient and three velocity components).
loss.weighting: Surface loss plus 0.2 times volume loss. Within each term every sampled cell and every channel carries equal weight: the loss is not weighted by surface face area or cell volume, and query cells are drawn uniformly by cell, not by area.

summary.notes: Geometry enters only through the NURBS description; the native meshes contribute cell-centre positions alone, as query points and as volume anchor positions. Every native cell is decoded directly, so every mapping is the identity with coverage 1.0 and no interpolation, nearest-neighbour assignment or extrapolation is applied. Surface and volume queries are decoded in chunks of 2000000, the last chunk of each holding the remainder; each forward pass decodes one surface chunk and one volume chunk against the same geometry and anchor context, recomputed from identical inputs, and query points are never attention keys, so chunking changes nothing beyond the run-to-run GPU rounding differences described in the method record.
